title: A finger-cuff waveform CNN screens for aortic stenosis in a multicenter cohort
summary: A one-dimensional convolutional model learned to identify at least moderate aortic stenosis from noninvasive finger-cuff arterial pressure waveforms, using echocardiography as reference. Development included 3,634 participants and evaluation used a temporally distinct multicenter cohort of 1,336 participants. In that cohort, significant stenosis screening had AUC 0.893, sensitivity 92.5%, specificity 64.5% and positive predictive value 36.4%. These are cohort diagnostic results, not evidence of improved patient outcomes. Prospective participant recruitment alone does not establish a frozen-model prospective evaluation; model-selection timing and full Methods were not assessed in the abstract review.
ai_technology: One-dimensional convolutional neural network for arterial pressure waveforms
organization: Cleveland Clinic Foundation; University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center; Edwards Lifesciences; Hospital Reina Sofia de Cordoba; Amsterdam UMC, University of Amsterdam

evidence.tested: Development cohort: 3,634 participants, 307 with significant stenosis; validation cohort: 1,336 participants, 241 with significant stenosis. Echo-referenced validation AUC 0.893, sensitivity 92.5%, specificity 64.5%, PPV 36.4%.
evidence.unknown: Full manuscript Methods, prespecification and locked-model timing not assessed. Low positive predictive value implies confirmatory testing remains relevant; outcome benefit and deployment effectiveness not established.
evidence.ai_role: A 1D convolutional network maps pressure waveforms to significant-stenosis classification; echocardiography supplied the diagnostic reference.

source_review.scope: Independent reading of original NCBI PubMed XML for the primary JACC article: complete structured Background/Objectives/Methods/Results/Conclusions, electronic publication date and author affiliations. Publisher DOI route was a redirect placeholder; no full manuscript/supplement read.
